body:
I've validated that there is a discrepancy with this. If [evidence returned is null](https://github.com/zaproxy/zaproxy/blob/2887f86fc7d0f4b74c31898dfabb52a432af17ad/src/org/zaproxy/zap/extension/api/CoreAPI.java#L1408) it isn't included. I verified this by listing 100 alerts, in which I encountered 70 occurrences of "evidence", when I changed that line to `String.valueOf(alert.getEvidence())` then I got 100 occurrences of "evidence" in my results (30 occurrences of "null").

Going forward we probably don't want "null" but rather just an empty string. But at last this identifies there where and the cause.

I checked through 100 alerts and only found `evidence` impacted, I then did a second set and found 2 occurrences of `attack` impacted. After that I went through a third set that confirmed the same but didn't reveal anything further.

Something like: `map.put("evidence", alert.getEvidence() == null ? "" : alert.getEvidence() );` might also be a workable solution.

So this can be handled in the API as mentioned above, however, I've been wondering if it would be better handled in the `Alert` class itself. Currently all the setElement type methods just return if the value being passed is null, I suggest that similar to above we check null and set empty string instead.

Thoughts?

<sub>Refs:
https://github.com/zaproxy/zaproxy/blob/develop/src/org/parosproxy/paros/core/scanner/Alert.java
https://github.com/zaproxy/zaproxy/blob/develop/src/org/zaproxy/zap/extension/api/CoreAPI.java</sub>

You mean for all setters or just for attack/evidence? I'm fine either way, but if the former we need to check if core or the add-ons are setting null values and tweak accordingly.
We still need to change CoreAPI to return always the `messageId`.

I hadn't decided one way or the other, just wanted to get the discussion started. 

There are definitely addons (rules) that set nulls for some elements when creating alerts. I guess they can be aligned to send empty strings, but I figured handling it centrally would work for those and for future cases as well (and any potential third party cases too).

Right, was not worried about the "bingo" methods but direct calls to the setters, probably we don't have any setting nulls (which would have a different behaviour if all the alert setters are changed to handle null as empty string).

Ok I see what you're getting at. I'll try to search around for direct use of the setters.

It looks like Eclipse has some functionality for finding references, so if I leverage that for each method do you think that provides good enough coverage?

Also am I missing something in this ticket or is there another one about the `messageId` being missing? Or is that something you've observed?

Don't mind tackling it but need to understand how/where it's happening.

Yeah, that should be enough.

That might happen but just on corner cases (e.g. an alert raised on a temporary message), I don't think there's any code change needed other than always add the field.

Oh it looks like it's this:
https://github.com/zaproxy/zaproxy/blob/develop/src/org/zaproxy/zap/extension/api/CoreAPI.java#L1481-L1483

Do we want to set `0` or `-1` for those edge cases? Because if there isn't a history ref (or if it's a temp message and the session is re-opened) there isn't a message to associate right?
Right. Maybe leave it empty? It does not need to be a number.

Using Eclipse references checking across ZAP and the extensions none of the following had occurences of specifically setting null: `setName`, `setURI`, `setDescription`, `setParam`, `setOtherInfo`, `setSolution`, `setReferences`, `setAttack`, `setEvidence`, `setCweId`, and `setWascId`.

issue.title: Issue API should always return all Alert elements

repository.name: zaproxy
repository.description: The ZAP by Checkmarx Core project

issue.body:
* `CoreAPI` ensure messageId is always included in API output.
* `Alert` ensure element setters set empty string if passed null. (So that all elements ultimately end up in API responses [even if empty strings]). Also cleaned up unnecessary `//ZAP` comments.

Fixes zaproxy/zaproxy#1984
